pll1d8c3-d1e3475.summary: States that the divine essence alone is properly and truly simple, having no diversity, variation, or multitude of parts, accidents, or forms.
claims: Only the divine essence is truly simple.
There is no diversity of parts, accidents, or forms in God.

pll1d8c3-d1e3478.summary: Following De Trinitate VI, shows why no creature is truly simple, starting with bodies: they have larger and smaller parts, the whole exceeds any part, and magnitude, color, and figure are distinct and can vary separately. So bodily nature is multiple.
claims: In bodies magnitude, color, and figure are distinct and separable.
Bodily nature is multiple, not simple.

pl-l1d8c3.summary: Asserts that the divine essence alone is properly and truly simple, without any diversity of parts, accidents, or forms. Following De Trinitate VI, it shows why bodily creatures are not simple: they have greater and lesser parts, and in them magnitude, color, and figure differ and vary independently.
claims: The divine essence alone is properly and truly simple.
In God there is no diversity of parts, accidents, or forms.
Bodily creatures are composite, made of parts and differing attributes.
